symptom: A user task's `targeting users xpath [System.User/Name = 'MxAdmin']` passed `check -p --references` and exec; Studio Pro reported CE0161 'Error(s) in XPath constraint' on every task carrying it (three of five workflows in an agent eval). `[NoSuchAttr = 'x']` and `[System.WorkflowGroup/Name = …]` on group targeting passed the same way. The same leading entity step in a microflow retrieve (`[Mod.Doc/Title = 'x']` on Mod.Doc) and a list view's database source passed check and were CE0161 too
cause: Nothing walked a targeting constraint: the expression-scope pass skipped it as 'not an expression' and the reference pass checked only a targeting microflow's name. The shared XPath member walk (walkPath) reads an entity as a FIRST path step as a cast and accepts it; a constraint is already evaluated on its entity, so mxbuild rejects that step. The System module has no domain model in the project, so the project resolver answers memberUnknown for every System.User member and could not have reported NoSuchAttr
file: `mdl/executor/validate_workflow_targeting_xpath.go` (new; wired into validateWorkflowStatementRefs and validateAlterWorkflowRefs), `mdl/executor/validate_widget_member_refs.go` (unresolvableXPathStepsAndLeadingEntity, leadingEntityStepMessage), `mdl/executor/validate_retrieve_members.go`, `cmd/mxcli/syntax/features_workflow.go` (examples), `mdl-examples/doctype-tests/24-workflow-examples.mdl`
insight: **mx check hides CE0161 behind any CE1613.** The first 11.15.0 run had one task with an unknown `[%UserRole_Manager%]` token (CE1613), and mx check then reported NO CE0161 anywhere in the app — not the bad targeting constraints, not an unrelated retrieve — which reads exactly like 'mxbuild 11.15 accepts these'. Dropping that one task surfaced four. Measure each rejected shape in an app with no other error, or one experiment per copy. Second: a retrieve-shaped check cannot be reused for targeting as is — the constraint's context is the workflow user entity (System.User or the App Settings specialization), whose System members exist only in modelsdk/meta; the system-aware model is local to this check because making the shared model know System entities would let noteQualified start judging System associations it cannot resolve. The access-rule caller keeps the plain walk: the same leading step in a grant was not rejected on that app (possibly the security level), so it is unmeasured there, not known-good Third: ANY entity as the first step is CE0161 (measured: the constrained entity, a specialization of it, an unrelated entity), but 'drop the step' is only the fix when it names the constrained entity or a generalization — the message offers it only then Fourth, likely the source: `mxcli syntax workflow.user-task(.targeting)` itself showed `[Module.Employee/Active = true()]` and `[HR.Employee/Role = …]` — the leading-entity shape the agent wrote as `[System.User/Name = …]`; grep the syntax help and doctype examples for a pattern before blaming the model. The doctype showcase's `[Status = 'Draft']` passed CI only because a later ALTER replaced it with microflow targeting before mx check ran (measured CE0161 on 11.12.2, CI's version)
fix: Check each targeting constraint as buildUserTask stores it (resolveXPathMemberNames) against the configured user entity / System.WorkflowGroup with a meta-backed model; report a leading entity step (CE0161, with the `[Member = …]` fix), a member the entity lacks (CE0161), and a missing association (CE1613). The walk reports a leading entity step only where opted in: retrieve, widget source, targeting
